correctness.rationale: Teh arXiv:2608.11500v1 Definition 3.1 conditions (C1)-(C5) are used with the correct inclusive Hare threshold. A voter type deficient at level ell and without an unelected approved candidate cannot contribute. Symmetrization reduces every witness to two nonnegative per-voter weights. For one type, minimal candidate weight is ell times that weight. If both types participate and a shared unelected candidate exists, EJR+ already fails. Otherwise Y is bounded below by ell(s+t)-r min(s,t), since only r elected shared candidates can share weight and each saves at most min(s,t). The bound is attained at (1,0),(0,1),(1,1), and on either half cone the relevant ratio is fractional-linear, so no interior maximum is missed. The four conditions follow by comparison to n/k. Supported-winner and Pareto-optimal corollaries are direct; the two-type separation has exact level-four weights with Y=6, Z=5, quota 5/6 and satisfies literal FJR and EJR+. An independent implementation of the source LP agreed with the criterion on 3852 exhaustively generated small cases and 1653 deterministic pseudorandom cases. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest full primary paper Teh (2026, arXiv:2608.11500v1) introduces FJR+, a general LP test, a strictness example on more than two ballot types, and party-list lower quota for disjoint approval sets, but does not state or imply an exact four-test characterization for two possibly overlapping ballot types or its collapse to EJR+ on Pareto-optimal committees. Dong and Peters (2026, arXiv:2605.04612v1) characterize EJR+ axiomatically and discuss FJR separately but do not study Teh's FJR+ test. Relevant previously recorded two-ballot work proves JUQ/JNQ/EJR+ existence, not the new FJR+ iff criterion. Bounded web, primary-source and published-finding corpus searches found no covering theorem, though worldwide novelty is not certified.

value.rationale: FJR+ is a new, meaningful fractional strengthening of representation in committee elections. An exact closed-form decision criterion on the first overlapping two-ballot domain reveals precisely when its extra fractional power matters, replacing a general LP and proving collapse to EJR+ for supported and Pareto-optimal committees. The two-type counterexample demonstrates that the support qualification is substantive, not cosmetic. This is a motivated structural boundary of a newly introduced fairness axiom and not a routine numerical recomputation. The result is intentionally limited to unweighted integral Hare-quota elections with two types.
